sections.label: Infrastructure & Utilities
sections.summary: Missing documentation for conductor clearances and inadequate transformer pad design, lacking protective measures, equipment specifications, and required approvals.

sections.label: Street Trees & Landscaping
sections.summary: Proposed trees violate utility clearances for overhead distribution lines and infrastructure; landscape documentation incomplete with missing species designations and clearance dimensions.

sections.label: Plan Documentation & Administrative
sections.summary: Construction safety notifications and staging area clearance documentation required.

comments.headline: Missing surveyed conductor elevations and clearance dimensions
comments.summary: Overhead electric lines are present on and adjacent to the site. Buildings and site structures lack surveyed conductor elevation data and dimensioned clearances required to verify horizontal (7.5-foot sky-to-ground, 15-foot radial) and vertical clearances per UCM § 1.10.3. Building elevation sheets and section/profile exhibits with conductor measurements are absent. Additionally, code prohibits installing customer facilities directly under or over distribution conductors—this cannot be verified without surveyed conductor routing.
comments.crossDep: Coordination with Austin Energy required to provide registered surveyor mid-span clearance measurements and conductor routing; may necessitate conductor relocation or building repositioning.
comments.attn: Verify whether overhead electric line on northern boundary (shown on Sheet 4 existing survey) is intended to be removed, relocated, or left in place. Current site plan (Sheet 9) omits this pole location entirely, creating ambiguity about design intent.

details.text: Buildings proposed near overhead lines on property boundaries lack surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimensions on building elevations or plans. Cannot verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained.

runComments.comment: Buildings are proposed on site with overhead electric lines on adjacent property boundaries. No surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimensions are shown on building elevation sheets or plan views to verify the 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained. Clearance verification exhibits are required.

Overhead electric lines exist on the property (shown on Sheet 4 existing survey), and buildings are proposed (Sheets 9, 21). However, no surveyed conductor elevations or horizontal clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to any building faces are provided. Measurement from conductor location (not pole centerline) required to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance cannot be determined without surveyor data showing conductor position relative to building setbacks.

Building locations shown on site plan with overhead electric line on southern boundary. No building elevation sheets provided showing surveyed conductor elevations or roof/eave elevations. Cannot verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance is maintained without these essential elevation views and dimension callouts.

details.text: Building projections (overhangs, eaves, balconies, roofs, patios) not shown on elevation sheets relative to overhead conductors. Required 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from projections cannot be assessed.

runComments.comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet plan set, preventing verification of overhangs, awnings, balconies, decks, roofs, or patios relative to overhead conductors. Both 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances for building projections cannot be assessed.

No building elevation sheets provided showing projections (overhangs, eaves, balconies, roofs, patios). Cannot verify required 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearances from building projections without elevation views.

details.text: Buildings 1 and 2 positioned within clearance distance of overhead utilities on Valley View Road right-of-way and northern boundary. Existing utilities shown on Sheet 4 but omitted from proposed site plan (Sheet 9) with no notation of removal, relocation, or retention. No surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimensions provided.

runComments.comment: Overhead utility lines exist in the right-of-way along Valley View Road (western boundary per Sheet 4), and buildings are proposed within potential clearance distance (Sheet 9). No surveyed conductor elevations or clearance dimensions from outside conductor to buildings are provided, preventing verification of required 7.5-foot and 15-foot clearances.

Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents overhead utility line on-site along northern property boundary. Proposed site plan (Sheet 9) omits northern overhead utilities with no demolition, relocation, or undergrounding notes. Cannot verify building setbacks from ROW and relocated facilities when existing utilities are not accounted for in proposed plan.

details.text: No building elevation sheets included in 39-sheet plan set showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations or clearance dimension callouts to building faces and projections. Required engineered, sealed elevation drawings demonstrating vertical clearances are absent.

runComments.comment: Building elevation sheets do not include surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors. Clearance verification requires registered surveyor data showing conductor elevations and clearance dimensions to building faces and projections. This is a required element per UCM § 1.10.3.

Building elevation sheets with surveyed conductor elevations and clearance dimension annotations are not included in the submitted site plan. The 39-sheet plan set contains no building elevation drawings. Per UCM § 1.10.3, engineered, sealed elevation drawings showing vertical relationships between overhead conductors and buildings, including all projections, with dimensioned clearances are required.

No building elevation sheets are included in the site plan set showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations or clearance dimensions to building faces and projections. This is a critical missing document type explicitly required by code to demonstrate vertical clearances from overhead electric conductors are met.

details.text: Section and plan view exhibits lack dimensions originating from outside conductor to building edges and projections. Clearance dimension lines must extend from outer conductor (not pole centerline or multi-conductor centerline). None provided.

runComments.comment: Section and plan view exhibits do not show dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings, building projections, or other site features. Clearance dimension annotations must originate from the outside conductor (not pole centerline) and extend to building edges and projections.

Site plan (Sheet 9) and electrical design plan (Sheet 21) show building locations and site features, but contain no dimension lines or annotations showing distances from outer electric conductors to building edges, projections, or other site features. Required section views and enlarged plan details with dimension lines originating from the outside conductor location are not provided.

No section or profile exhibits provided showing clearance dimensions from outer conductor to building edges, projections, or other site features. Plans show buildings and overhead lines in plan view only with no cross-section documentation of vertical and horizontal relationships or clearance dimensions.

details.text: No clearance dimensions shown on any plan sheets. All required dimensions must originate from outside conductor location; on multi-conductor installations, outermost conductor may be several feet offset from pole center. Dimension methodology absent.

runComments.comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets. Where clearances are required to be dimensioned, the dimension lines must extend from the outside conductor (not from utility pole centerline or pole structure). On multi-conductor installations, the outermost conductor may be several feet offset from pole center.

Dimension lines and clearance annotations on submitted plans show distances from property lines, easement boundaries, and pole locations, but do not originate from the outside conductor location. Per UCM § 1.10.3 and the measurement methodology in the regulatory overview, all clearances must be measured from the outside conductor (the actual electric wire), not from utility pole centerline or easement boundaries. On multi-conductor installations, the outermost conductor may be several feet offset from pole center. Dimension lines must explicitly show origin at conductor position.

Plans show overhead lines but provide no clearance dimension callouts measuring distances from features to overhead conductors. Code requires clearance dimensions extend from outside conductor (not pole centerline or centerline of multi-conductor lines), yet no dimensions are provided to verify this measurement methodology. Cannot verify compliance when dimensions are completely absent.

details.text: Code establishes absolute prohibition against installing customer facilities (buildings, driveways, structures) under or over Austin Energy distribution conductors. Plans show buildings and driveways near/under overhead lines with no explicit documentation confirming facilities are not placed directly beneath/over conductors.

runComments.comment: Overhead distribution lines and electric easements (5-foot easements) are shown on existing conditions survey (Sheet 4). Buildings are positioned within electric easement areas on the site plan (Sheet 9). Without surveyed conductor routing and exact clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to all buildings and site features within the easement, it cannot be definitively verified that customer facilities are not installed beneath or over distribution conductors (absolute prohibition per UCM § 1.10.3) or that 7.5-foot clearance is maintained for items within easements.

Code establishes absolute prohibition against installing customer facilities (buildings, driveways, structures) under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, independent of clearance distances. Plans show driveways crossing under southern overhead line and buildings near overhead facilities. No explicit documentation confirms facilities are not placed directly beneath/over conductors. Cannot confirm compliance with absolute prohibition.

details.text: Building finished floor elevations (686.25–685 ft MSL) shown; overhead conductor elevations unknown. Without surveyed conductor heights and building roof elevations, vertical clearances cannot be verified and appear marginal. Registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey and site-specific analysis required but not provided.

runComments.comment: No registered surveyor data showing pole locations and mid-span conductor clearances is provided on any submitted sheet. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows surveyed pole locations, but no conductor elevation data. When overhead facilities cross proposed site features (buildings, driveways, parking), surveyed mid-span clearance measurements are required to verify vertical clearances meet minimum requirements. These measurements are absent from the plan set.

Building finished floor elevations range 686.25-685 ft MSL; overhead conductor elevations unknown. Without surveyed conductor heights and building roof elevations, vertical clearances cannot be verified and appear marginal. Code requires registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey and site-specific analysis when vertical clearance requirements may not be met. This critical survey and analysis are not provided despite marginal clearance conditions.

comments.headline: Missing vertical clearance verification for driveways and transformer
comments.summary: Driveways are proposed to cross under overhead electric lines, and a transformer pad is shown near overhead distribution lines. No vertical clearance dimensions from the lowest point of overhead conductors (including attachments) to finished driveway/parking grades or to the transformer pad are provided. Mid-span surveyed clearance heights and determination of truck-traffic applicability are absent, preventing verification of minimum 15-foot (transformer radial) or 16/18-foot (driveway vertical) clearance requirements per UCM § 1.10.3 and § 1.10.6.2.
comments.crossDep: Coordination with Austin Energy required for registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey; may necessitate grading adjustments, driveway rerouting, or conductor relocation.
comments.attn: Clarify whether any internal driveways will accommodate truck traffic (garbage collection, emergency response, delivery, etc.). This determines minimum clearance requirement (16-foot vs. 18-foot).

details.text: Transformer pad shown near overhead distribution lines on property boundaries. No clearance dimensions from outside conductor provided. Required 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductor in all directions cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad is shown on the site plan with overhead electric distribution lines on property boundaries, but no clearance dimensions from the outside conductor are provided. The required 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors cannot be verified from the available plans.

Distribution overhead conductors shown on existing conditions survey (Sheet 4); buildings and facilities proposed throughout site (Sheets 9, 21). Without surveyed conductor locations and radial clearance dimensions, the 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductor in all directions cannot be verified. No profile drawings show radial clearance envelopes.

Overhead electric line documented on southern boundary. Building locations shown but no clearance dimensions provided. Cannot verify 15-foot radial clearance without dimension callouts, conductor identification (primary/secondary/neutral), and voltage specifications.

details.text: Internal driveways and parking areas proposed crossing under overhead electric line on southern boundary. No vertical clearance dimensions from lowest conductor (including attachments) to finished grades provided. Truck-traffic determination (16-foot vs. 18-foot minimum) not made. Registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey not provided.

runComments.comment: Internal driveways and parking areas are proposed (Sheets 9, 11). Overhead utility lines exist on property boundaries (Sheet 4). No vertical clearance dimensions from the lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attachments) to finished driveway/parking grades are provided. Verification of 16-foot minimum (parking without trucks) or 18-foot (areas with truck traffic) clearance requires surveyed conductor elevation data and grading section exhibits not provided.

Site plan shows proposed driveways crossing under overhead electric line on southern boundary. No vertical clearance dimensions provided on grading plan, profile sections, or utility plan. No determination whether truck traffic applies (16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement). No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data provided. Cannot verify driveways maintain minimum vertical clearance from lowest point of overhead facilities including any telecommunications attachments.

comments.headline: Missing AE Design approvals and easement documentation
comments.summary: Required Austin Energy Design approvals, transformer easements, and recorded easement depictions are not provided. Compliance with AE Design standards and verification that pads avoid conflict with existing utility easements cannot be confirmed.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy Design and Legal/Real Estate — new transformer easements require AE coordination and legal review; recorded easement compliance requires property records verification.
comments.attn: Verify recorded easement locations per facts.md. Two critical unrecorded easements affect NE portion of site: Greenbelt Access & Use (0.31 acres) and City of Austin Drainage (0.130 acres).

details.text: Transformer pad dimensions are not labeled on electrical plan and no AE Design-approved detail sheets are provided. Pad dimensions must match AE Design-approved specifications for specified service type (single/three-phase) and equipment load.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad dimensions are not shown on the submitted electrical plan. No Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets (which specify pad dimensions based on service type and equipment specifications) are included in the site plan submission. Provide AE Design approval letter and transformer pad detail sheets confirming pad dimensions match the specifications for the proposed service type (single-phase or three-phase).

Transformer pad dimensions are not shown on the electrical plan, and no Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets have been provided or referenced. Pad dimensions must match AE Design-approved details for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase) and equipment load.

Transformer pad dimensions are not labeled or dimensioned on the electrical plan. No reference callouts to Austin Energy Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets are provided. Compliance with AE Design pad specifications for the specified service type cannot be verified.

details.text: Transformer easements for all five proposed pads are not depicted on any plan sheet. Easement boundaries and widths required to accommodate Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance operations are not specified.

runComments.comment: No transformer easements are depicted on the electrical plan, site plan, or easement exhibits. Transformer easements are required around all five proposed transformer pads to provide adequate access for Austin Energy Design operations and maintenance, and the required easement widths have not been specified.

Transformer easements are not shown on any of the site plan sheets. No easement boundaries or widths are depicted around the transformer pads to accommodate Austin Energy accessibility and maintenance requirements.

details.text: Transformer pad southeast of Buildings 6–7 is 5.2 feet from Building 7 wall, at the minimum threshold. If reduced clearance below 5 feet is proposed, AE Design written approval and verification of required conditions (not in confined space, adequate window/door/duct clearance, 3-hour fire rating) must be documented.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad between Buildings 6 and 7 is located at 5.2 feet from Building 7 wall (at the 5-foot minimum threshold). If this clearance is claimed as reduced clearance (less than 5 feet to brick/masonry), documentation of Austin Energy Design written approval and verification of required conditions (not in confined space, adequate window/door/duct clearance, 3-hour fire rating) must be provided. Cannot verify clearance compliance status from available documents.

details.text: Two critical recorded easements not depicted on site plan: Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731, 0.31 acres NE interior) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137, 0.130 acres NE corner). Transformer pad locations relative to these and all recorded utility easements cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: According to facts.md, two critical easements are recorded but NOT depicted on the submitted site plan: (1) Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (Instrument 2010070731) covering 0.31 acres in NE interior, and (2) City of Austin Drainage Easement (Instrument 2011021137) covering 0.130 acres in NE corner. Specific confirmation that all five transformer pads are located outside drainage easements, water easements, sewer easements, and electrical easements under overhead lines cannot be verified without proper easement depiction on plans.

comments.headline: Inadequate clearances from transformer pads to utility infrastructure
comments.summary: Transformer pads lack documented minimum clearances to water, wastewater, storm drain, and other underground utilities. Some pads violate the 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance requirement. Cross-sections showing vertical utility relationships are not provided.
comments.crossDep: Utility Departments (Water, Wastewater, Stormwater) — Clearance conflicts may require utility line relocation or pad relocation, requiring coordination with utility providers.
comments.attn: Run 1 findings indicate confirmed clearance violations (Pads 2 and 3 to water line; Pads 1 and 2 to wastewater line). Verify current utility routing and pad coordinates; confirm corrective action in revised plans.

details.text: Transformer Pad 2 (mid-western side yard near Building 2) is 0.9 feet from nearest water line; Pad 3 (southwest area near Building 8) has zero clearance/overlaps water line. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance required. Dimensioned clearances must be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer Pad 2 (mid-western side yard near Building 2) is located only 0.9 feet from the nearest water line; Transformer Pad 3 (southwest area near Building 8) has zero clearance/overlaps with the water line. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance required. Relocate pads or reroute water lines to achieve required clearance.

Water utility lines are shown on utility and electrical plans but no specific dimensioned clearances are marked between water lines and transformer pad locations. Cannot verify minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to water infrastructure.

details.text: Transformer Pad 1 (northwest entrance near Building 1) is 4.6 feet from wastewater line; Pad 2 (mid-western side yard near Building 2) is 2.5 feet from wastewater line. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance required from all sides. Dimensioned clearances must be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer Pad 1 (northwest entrance area near Building 1) is located 4.6 feet from the nearest wastewater line; Transformer Pad 2 (mid-western side yard near Building 2) is 2.5 feet from wastewater line. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance required from all sides. Relocate pads or reroute wastewater lines to achieve required clearance.

Wastewater utility lines are shown on utility and electrical plans but no specific dimensioned clearances are marked between wastewater lines and transformer pad locations. Cannot verify minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to wastewater infrastructure.

details.text: Storm drain infrastructure routing relative to transformer pads lacks dimensioned clearance markings. Minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Storm drain lines are shown on site plan but no specific dimensioned clearances are marked between storm drain infrastructure and transformer pad locations. Cannot verify minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from transformer pads to storm drain lines.

details.text: Specific dimensioned clearances between transformer pads and multiple underground utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain, electric) are not marked on any plan. Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from pads to other utilities cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Multiple underground utilities are shown on site (water, wastewater, storm drain, electric) but specific dimensioned clearances between transformer pads and other underground utilities are not marked on any plan. Cannot verify minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from transformer pads to other underground utilities.

details.text: Cross-section or profile drawings showing vertical clearances from transformer pad locations to overhead structures, parking garages, and enclosed areas are not provided. Vertical clearance compliance cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer pads are located within site development area with buildings and structures in close proximity. No cross-section or profile drawings are provided showing vertical clearances from transformer pad locations to any overhead structures, parking structures, or enclosed areas. Cannot verify vertical clearance compliance.

No cross-section drawings are provided showing vertical clearances in access paths or demonstrating clearances to any overhead structures, parking garages, or enclosed areas associated with transformer locations. Vertical clearance compliance cannot be verified.

details.text: Profile or cross-section drawings showing vertical relationships between transformer pads and utility lines are not provided. Confirmation that pads and Austin Energy underground facilities are not located over/under other utility lines cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Plans show multiple utility lines crossing throughout the site. Profile or cross-section drawings showing vertical relationships between transformer pads and utility lines are not provided. Cannot confirm that transformer pads or Austin Energy underground facilities are not located over or under other utility lines, and that customer buildings/foundations/structures are not installed over Austin Energy underground facilities.

comments.headline: Missing bollard protection for vehicle-proximate transformer pads
comments.summary: Two transformer pads are located within 4 feet of vehicle circulation routes. Equipment within 4 feet of parking areas requires 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized bollards per AE Design standards. No bollards are shown or specified.

details.text: Transformer pad between Buildings 4–5 is 4.1 feet from central drive aisle. Transformer pad south of Building 7 is 3.2 feet from nearest vehicle circulation route. Both within 4-foot threshold requiring 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal post bollards. No bollards shown or specified.

runComments.comment: Transformer pad located between Buildings 4 and 5 is positioned 4.1 feet from the central drive aisle (vehicle route). Equipment installed within 4 feet of parking areas or vehicle circulation routes requires 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal post bollards per AE Design pad details. No bollards are shown or noted on the electrical plan or detail sheets, and no bollard specifications or locations are provided.

The transformer pad in the south area (near Building 7) is located 3.2 feet from the nearest vehicle circulation route, which is within the 4-foot threshold requiring bollard protection. No 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized bollards are shown on the electrical plan or any detail sheets. Bollards are required per AE Design equipment pad specifications.

comments.headline: Overhead distribution trees violate clearance distances
comments.summary: Proposed Cedar Elm and Live Oak trees are positioned 0–6 feet from the overhead electrical conductor along the southern boundary. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires 15 feet minimum for distribution lines and 25 feet for trees exceeding 40 feet mature height. No Austin Energy approval for non-compliant placements is documented.

details.text: Cedar Elm and Live Oak (non-utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F) are positioned 0–6 feet from overhead distribution conductor, violating 15-foot minimum clearance. Species utility-compatibility not explicitly verified on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: Proposed trees are positioned 0-1.5 feet from overhead electric (OHE) distribution line on southern boundary. Utility-compatibility status of specific tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) cannot be conclusively determined from submitted plans to verify whether species are marked as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F. ECM Appendix F UC column designation not provided.

Landscape plan shows proposed trees at 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor running along southern property boundary. Cedar Elm (non-utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F) and Live Oak (non-utility-compatible) specified on plant schedule are proposed as part of the mitigation trees. Trees must be repositioned to maintain minimum 15 lateral feet from outside conductor per UCM § 1.10.10.4, or species must be changed to utility-compatible alternatives.

Trees are shown planted along the southern site boundary within approximately 5-10 feet of the overhead electric line (based on graphic scale 1"=20'). However, the landscape plan does not identify the species of these trees, so utility-compatible status per ECM Appendix F cannot be verified. Plant species schedule exists on Sheet 35 but is not cross-referenced to specific locations on the landscape plan. Provide species identification labels on the landscape plan for all trees proposed within 25 feet of overhead electric facilities.

details.text: Cedar Elm (90 ft mature) and Live Oak (60 ft mature) exceed 40-foot height threshold requiring 25 feet lateral clearance from distribution conductors. Measured distances of 0–6 feet represent violations of 19–25 feet.

runComments.comment: Large trees with mature height 40+ feet (Cedar Elm and Live Oak per ECM Appendix F) are proposed at 0-1.5 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires minimum 25 lateral feet clearance. Measured distances: 0 feet (westernmost), 1.5 feet (central), 0 feet (easternmost).

Proposed large trees (Cedar Elm at 90 feet mature height, Live Oak at 60 feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are located 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor. Large trees require minimum 25 lateral feet clearance from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Trees must be repositioned or replaced with trees of compliant mature height (less than 40 feet).

Large trees (mature height 40+ feet) cannot be verified as meeting the 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors because the landscape plan does not identify which species are planted at which locations. While Live Oak and Cedar Elm are shown in the plant schedule with 16-foot minimum heights, their mature heights per ECM Appendix F cannot be verified against specific planting locations on the site plan. Provide species identification and mature height notation on landscape plan for all proposed trees.

details.text: No documented written approval from Austin Energy is provided for trees positioned within prohibited clearance zones or utilizing non-utility-compatible species. Variations require explicit Austin Energy approval per UCM § 1.10.10.4.

runComments.comment: Plans propose trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) within prohibited clearance zones: trees within 15-25 feet of overhead distribution conductors and within 10 feet of utility poles and transformer equipment. No documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing these variations is provided or referenced on the plans, in the site plan notes, or in the submitted documents.

Landscape plan proposes trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) within prohibited clearance zones (less than 15 feet from distribution conductors and less than 25 feet for large trees) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Variations to standard tree placement distances and non-compatible species designations require explicit Austin Energy approval per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide signed approval letter from Austin Energy or revise landscape plan to maintain required clearances.

comments.headline: Trees violate clearance from utility poles and transformer pads
comments.summary: Proposed trees are measured 1.7–8.5 feet from utility poles and transformer pads, violating UCM § 1.10.10.4 minimum 10-foot lateral clearance. Additionally, poles and transformer access doors are not clearly identified or cross-referenced on the landscape plan.
comments.crossDep: Austin Energy for utility pole locations and transformer pad access requirements.

details.text: Proposed tree measured 8.5 lateral feet from utility pole centerline, violating minimum 10-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Utility poles are not clearly identified or labeled on electrical (Sheet 21) or landscape (Sheet 31) plans, preventing verification of all tree-to-pole distances.

runComments.comment: Proposed tree measured at 8.5 lateral feet from overhead electric utility pole. UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of poles. Tree location is 1.5 feet closer than minimum required distance.

Electrical utility poles are not clearly identified or labeled on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) or landscape plan (Sheet 31). Proposed trees must maintain minimum 10 lateral feet from utility pole centerlines per UCM § 1.10.10.4, but this cannot be verified from submitted plans. Provide pole locations and identify all utility poles on the landscape plan with tree locations relative to poles clearly dimensioned or noted.

details.text: Proposed tree measured 1.7 lateral feet from pad-mounted transformer equipment access door, violating minimum 10-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Transformer pad locations (west of Buildings 2, 8 and east of Buildings 4, 7) shown on electrical plan are not cross-referenced on landscape plan.

runComments.comment: Proposed tree measured at 1.7 lateral feet from pad-mounted electrical transformer equipment. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires minimum 10 lateral feet clearance from pad-mounted equipment or between equipment access door and drivable surface. Tree position violates distance requirement by 8.3 feet.

Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations (west of Buildings 2 and 8, east of Buildings 4 and 7), but landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not provide cross-reference or clear notation showing tree locations relative to transformer access doors. Trees must maintain 10 lateral feet from pad-mounted equipment access doors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimension or cross-sheet reference showing tree clearances from transformer pads.

comments.headline: Missing transformer equipment specifications and pad drainage documentation
comments.summary: Transformer specifications do not identify equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type). Grading plan does not show surface drainage flow direction at transformer pad locations. Operational compliance cannot be verified.
comments.crossDep: Electrical Engineer and Civil Engineer (Grading) — Equipment type specification and drainage slope direction require coordination.
comments.attn: Transformer equipment specifications must clearly identify whether oil-filled or dry-type. If oil-filled, grading plan must show surface drainage flow direction at pad locations with slope percentages and 20-foot clearance from fire escapes.

details.text: Transformer pad access door orientation is not indicated on electrical plan. Required 10-foot minimum clearance to open area for hot-stick use cannot be verified. South pad is 5.9 feet from Building 7; if access door faces this building, 10-foot requirement would not be met.

runComments.comment: Electrical plan does not identify transformer access door orientation or show the hot-stick use area boundary (minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure required). Cannot verify whether the access door sides of all five transformer pads have adequate clearance to open area or confirm hot-stick use area compliance.

Transformer pad access door orientation is not indicated on the electrical plan. Without door orientation, the required 10-foot minimum clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure cannot be verified. The south pad is 5.9 feet from Building 7; if the access door faces this building, the 10-foot requirement would not be met.

details.text: Transformer specifications do not indicate whether equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. Grading plan does not show surface drainage flow direction around pads. For oil-filled transformers, verification that drainage slopes direct liquid flow away from buildings cannot be confirmed.

runComments.comment: Transformer specifications do not indicate whether equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. Grading plan does not show surface drainage flow direction around transformer pads. If oil-filled transformers are proposed, verification that surface drainage and grading slopes direct liquid flow away from buildings (minimum 20-foot horizontal clearance from fire escapes also required) cannot be confirmed from available plans.

details.text: Equipment type specification (oil-filled or dry-type) is missing from transformer data. Grading plan shows general site drainage but does not mark drainage flow direction specifically at pad locations. Surface drainage slope away from buildings cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer specifications do not identify whether equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. Grading plan shows general site drainage but does not mark drainage flow direction specifically at transformer pad locations. Cannot verify that surface drainage slopes direct liquid flow away from buildings (required for oil-filled transformers per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4 footnote 1).

comments.headline: Missing building elevation documentation for clearance verification
comments.summary: Building elevation drawings showing window, door, and ventilating duct locations, heights from grade, and lateral distances to transformer pads are not provided. Cannot verify 12-foot horizontal clearance and 5-foot lateral separation requirements.
comments.crossDep: Architect — Building elevations must show window, door, and duct locations with heights and lateral distances from transformer pads.
comments.attn: Architect must provide elevation drawings with dimensioned window/door/duct locations and heights. Verify compliance with 12-foot horizontal clearance (when openings are within 12 feet of grade) and 5-foot lateral separation requirements.

details.text: Adjacent multi-story residential buildings (1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8) lack elevation documentation showing window, door, and duct heights and lateral separations from transformer pads. Compliance with 12-foot horizontal clearance and 5-foot lateral separation cannot be verified.

runComments.comment: Transformer pads are adjacent to multi-story residential buildings (Buildings 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, and 8). Building elevation drawings showing window, door, and ventilating duct locations, heights from grade, and lateral separation distances relative to transformer pads are not provided. Cannot verify compliance with 12-foot horizontal clearance requirement when windows/doors are less than 12 feet from grade or have less than 5-foot lateral separation.

comments.headline: Utility pole locations, guy wires, and associated clearances undocumented
comments.summary: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) documents utility poles on northern and southern property boundaries. Proposed site plan (Sheet 9) omits pole locations with no notation of removal, relocation, or retention. No down guy wires, anchor locations, or associated clearances are shown. Proposed site features (fences, retaining walls, driveways, sidewalks) do not show clearance dimensions to pole locations. Down guy anchor easements required for distribution poles are not depicted on easement exhibits. Cannot verify that pole-related infrastructure conflicts are addressed or that clearances to poles and guy anchors are maintained.
comments.crossDep: Coordination with Austin Energy required to confirm pole retention, relocation, or removal; verify down guy locations, anchor easement requirements, and clearance zones for all proposed site features.
comments.attn: Contact Austin Energy directly to obtain registered surveyor documentation of pole locations, guy wire routing, anchor locations, and any required easements. Confirm whether northern boundary pole (Sheet 4) is on-site or off-site, and design intent (retain or relocate). Re-verify all clearances after pole status is confirmed.

details.text: Fences proposed throughout property perimeter near existing utility poles (Sheet 4). Exact measured distances between proposed fence post locations and pole locations not provided. Cannot verify 10-foot minimum horizontal clearance to poles.

runComments.comment: Fences are proposed (noted on landscape plan Sheet 31 and landscape calculations Sheet 35), including wooden privacy fences. Existing utility poles are shown on the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) at multiple property boundaries. Without exact measured distances between proposed fence post locations and existing pole locations, the 10-foot minimum horizontal clearance cannot be verified.

comments.headline: Proposed trees lack utility-compatible species designation
comments.summary: Landscape plan shows mitigation trees planted within 10–15 feet of overhead distribution conductor on southern property boundary. Code requires trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution conductors be Utility Compatible species (ECM Appendix F, typically mature height ≤ 20 feet, marked UC). Specific species of proposed mitigation trees are not confirmed on landscape plan, preventing verification that non-compatible species will not be planted. Non-compatible species will grow into overhead conductors, creating safety hazard.
comments.crossDep: Coordination with City Arborist and Austin Energy recommended to finalize tree species selection and confirm utility-compatible designations.
comments.attn: Provide a marked-up landscape plan identifying specific species for each tree location, cross-referenced to the plant schedule. Include ECM Appendix F utility-compatible verification for all trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead conductors.

details.text: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows mitigation trees (M symbols) planted 10–15 feet from southern overhead line. Landscape calculations (Sheet 35) list species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), but species-to-location cross-reference cannot be made. Without confirmed species identification, utility-compatible status (per ECM Appendix F) cannot be verified for trees within required 10-foot buffer.

runComments.comment: Landscape plan shows mitigation trees (marked 'M') planted within close proximity to overhead electric line on southern property boundary (approximately 4 trees in southeast corner area). The specific species of these mitigation trees are not identified on the landscape plan, making it impossible to verify whether they are utility-compatible species per ECM Appendix F. Trees within 10 lateral feet of distribution conductors or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors must be from the Utility Compatible list. Provide plant schedule identifying each mitigation tree species and verify compliance with utility-compatible requirements.

details.text: Overhead electric line and tree symbols visible on landscape plan but not dimensioned. Add dimension lines showing clearance distances from tree trunk centers to outside conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4 measurement methodology (15-foot distribution, 50-foot transmission minimums).

comments.headline: Missing construction safety notifications and staging area clearances
comments.summary: Plans do not include required notice that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before any work begins near high-voltage overhead lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003. No construction logistics or staging plan is provided documenting equipment laydown zones, work platforms, or crane operation areas maintain minimum 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333 and UCM § 1.10.2. These construction-phase requirements are separate from permanent clearances and must be addressed in plan notes and construction administration protocols.
comments.crossDep: Coordination with Safety/Construction Administration to finalize construction notification language and staging area logistics. Austin Energy and electrical contractor sign-off may be required.
comments.attn: Add explicit note to cover sheet or Sheet 3 (General Notes) stating: 'Owner/Contractor must notify Austin Energy at minimum 48 hours before any work begins near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.' Additionally, require construction staging plan or logistics exhibit showing equipment laydown zones and work platforms maintain 10-foot radial clearance from all energized overhead lines.

details.text: No construction logistics, staging plan, or equipment operation zones provided on site plans. Mandatory separate requirement from permanent clearances. Plans must include logistics plan or note addressing construction phase clearances.
